On Sun, May 31, 2026 at 9:12 AM Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Quick ask: please reply with your 1) numeric scores (Tech / System Design / Culture, scale 1-5), 2) top 2 strengths, and 3) any red flags by EOD Monday.

Scores (my interview — backend/task queue + debugging):
- Technical: 4/5
- System Design: 3/5
- Culture: 4/5

Top strengths:
- Very practical debugging approach; used real production examples.
- Clear ownership instinct; asked good questions about observability.

Potential red flags:
- Limited exposure to our preferred async patterns (RabbitMQ -> Celery-like flow). Could ramp quickly but will need handoff time.

I recommended: take-home assignment focused on designing a small job queue with retry semantics — helps test async design and edge cases.

Laura

Quick note — thanks everyone. My scores (coding + reliability):
- Technical: 2/5
- System Design: 3/5
- Culture: 4/5

I observed that Davion struggled with a few edge cases we commonly face in production (idempotency, partial failures). That's something we can't paper over.

I'd be comfortable doing the take-home if the task explicitly exercises failure handling and observability. If we see the same gaps there, I'm inclined to pass.

Vivek
SRE Manager

Thanks — consolidated the inputs into the attached master sheet (panel_scores_master.xlsx). Summary so far: Technical avg 3.2/5, Design avg 3.4/5, Culture avg 4.2/5.

Proposal:
- Run a focused take-home (48hr window) that covers async job retries, idempotency, and logging hooks. I'll draft the brief.
- Quick async poll: are you ok with that path or prefer manager final now? Reply with "TAKE-HOME" or "MANAGER-FINAL".

Proposed sync window (30 min) if anyone wants to talk before we deploy the take-home: Tue 6/2 10:00–12:00 or Tue 6/2 15:00–16:00 PT. I've added a tentative calendar placeholder.

Attachments: panel_scores_master.xlsx

Monica

TAKE-HOME for me.

Quick summary / reasoning: majority of the panel flagged implementation gaps but not cultural fit; a focused assignment will give us objective signal on failure modes and observability. If he passes the assignment with clear attention to idempotency and retries, I support moving to a final manager sync or direct offer depending on quality. If not, we close.

Agree with Hannah that we can skip an extra long panel if the take-home is strong.
